name: Whole Wheat Atta
description: Finely milled whole wheat flour (godhi hittu in Kannada) for soft chapati, phulka and poori, and for the wheat dosa and holige made in North Karnataka homes. A 5 kg pack gives a family of four roughly three to four weeks of daily chapatis.

name: Basmati Rice
description: Long-grain, fragrant basmati rice that cooks up long and separate, kept in Karnataka homes for biryani, ghee rice, pulao and festival meals rather than daily rice. A 1 kg pack covers two or three special-occasion meals for a family.

name: Salt
description: Iodised free-flowing table salt, called uppu in Kannada, used for everyday cooking, pickling and seasoning. A 1 kg pack is the standard household size and lasts a family several weeks.

name: Noodles
description: Instant masala noodles: a dried noodle cake with a spice sachet, ready in a couple of minutes on the stove. The 70 g single pack makes one bowl and is a common quick breakfast or after-school snack, often cooked with chopped onion, tomato and green chilli.

name: Biscuits - Glucose
description: Plain, lightly sweet glucose biscuits, the everyday tea-time biscuit in most Karnataka homes and dunked in chai or coffee. A 300 g pack keeps a family in biscuits for about a week and is the size usually kept in the kitchen tin.

name: Potato Chips
description: Thin fried potato crisps in a foil pack, sold in salted, masala and chilli-lime flavours. The 52 g pack is the twenty-rupee size that goes into school bags and bus journeys and is enough for one or two people.

name: Detergent Powder
description: Washing powder for laundry, used for both bucket hand-washing and washing machines. A 1 kg pack covers a small family's clothes for roughly two to three weeks.

name: Turmeric Powder
description: Ground dried turmeric root, called arishina in Kannada, added by the pinch to almost every sambar, palya, rasam and rice dish for colour and flavour. A 100 g pack lasts a family a month or two of daily cooking.

name: Sugar
description: White crystal sugar, called sakkare in Kannada, used for tea, coffee, payasa and festival sweets. A 1 kg pack suits a small family for two to three weeks of daily tea and cooking.

name: Rusk
description: Twice-baked slices of sweet bread, crisp and dry, usually with a hint of cardamom or sooji. Rusk is dunked in tea or coffee in the morning and evening; a 300 g pack holds about 25 to 30 slices and lasts a small family a week or two.

name: Coriander Powder
description: Ground dried coriander seed, called kothambari pudi in Kannada, used as the body of sambar, saaru and vegetable gravies and often mixed with chilli powder at the stove. A 100 g pack covers a small family's cooking for three to four weeks.

name: Sona Masoori Rice
description: Sona Masoori is the medium-grain, lightly aromatic rice that most Karnataka homes cook every day, and much of it is milled around Gangavathi, close to Hospet. Steamed (boiled) sona masoori cooks fluffy and separate, suits plain rice, bisi bele bath and pulao, and a 5 kg bag lasts a small family two to three weeks.

name: Sona Masoori Rice
description: The same everyday medium-grain sona masoori rice in a full 25 kg mill bag, the size most households around Hospet buy for the month. Steamed sona masoori cooks light and separate for plain rice, chitranna and bisi bele bath; a 25 kg bag lasts a family of four roughly a month to six weeks.

name: Idli Rice
description: Short, plump parboiled rice (idli akki in Kannada) that is soaked and ground with urad dal for soft idli and dosa batter. A 5 kg bag keeps a family in idli and dosa batter for about a month of weekend breakfasts.

name: Whole Wheat Atta
description: Whole wheat flour (godhi hittu) in a 10 kg bag for households that make chapati or roti every day, along with poori, paratha and holige. A 10 kg bag lasts a family of four about six to eight weeks and works out cheaper per kilo than smaller packs.

name: Jaggery
description: Unrefined cane sugar in solid blocks, called bella in Kannada, used to sweeten holige, payasa, kadubu and everyday coffee in many Karnataka homes. A 1 kg block or bag covers a family's festival cooking and a few weeks of daily use.

name: Chilli Powder
description: Ground dried red chillies, called menasina pudi in Kannada, the main source of heat in sambar, gojju, chutney pudi and non-veg gravies. A 200 g pack suits a family that cooks spicy food daily and lasts about a month.

name: Cumin Seeds
description: Whole cumin seed, called jeerige in Kannada, used in tempering for rasam, upma, pulao and jeera rice, and roasted and ground into fresh masala. A 100 g pack keeps a family's spice box stocked for a month or more.

name: Biscuits - Marie
description: Thin, crisp, mildly sweet Marie biscuits that are served with tea and coffee across Karnataka and are the usual biscuit offered to guests. A 250 g family pack holds about 45 biscuits, a week or so of tea-time for a small household.

name: Biscuits - Cream
description: Sandwich biscuits with a sweet cream filling, most often chocolate (bourbon) or vanilla and orange. A 150 g sleeve is the standard pocket-money pack picked up for school tiffins and evening tea in Karnataka homes.

name: Namkeen Mixture
description: Savoury snack mix of fried sev, boondi, peanuts, flattened rice and dal, spiced and salted. Mixture is the standard evening snack with coffee in Karnataka and is put out for guests; a 200 g pouch fills a snack bowl three or four times.
